Parrondo's Paradox

ParadoxesGame Strategy

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: watch your money go up or down in two bad games, then mix them and see if the mix can win.
How to play: set the sliders, type letter patterns like AB or ABBAB (or a chance like .4), and press Go. The chart shows the average money after many tries.
0.005 0.5 0.1 0.75 100 500 3
Look for the math

Parrondo's paradox says two losing games can be combined into a winning one. The chart averages many random walks of capital, just as the cut-the-knot applet did.

Game A and game B

Game A is a single coin: you win $1 with probability P and lose $1 otherwise. At the applet's defaults, P = 0.5 − ε with ε = 0.005, so A drifts down. Game B switches between two coins by your current capital: if capital is a multiple of M, use the poor coin P1; otherwise use the rich coin P2. With P1 = 0.1 − ε and P2 = 0.75 − ε, B alone still loses for M = 2 or 3, and wins for M > 3 — the logic test confirmed that split with Monte Carlo trials.

Mixing the losers

A mix plays A or B on each step. A string such as AB or ABBAB repeats that pattern; a number such as .4 picks A with that probability (and B otherwise). The applet compares A, B and up to seven mixes on one chart. For the default probabilities, ABBAB is the strongest among the usual patterns when M = 3, while AB leads when M = 2 or M = 4 — matching the page's claim and Zeilberger's results, again checked by the logic test.

Why the ratchet works

Game B is a capital-dependent ratchet: the poor coin is played only on a sparse set of capitals (multiples of M). Playing A in between shakes the capital off those bad residues often enough that the rich coin is used more, and the mixture can climb even though each pure game falls. Changing ε alone in the applet only updates the label — the live probabilities stay until you move P, P1 or P2 — and this port keeps that quirk.

Try M = 3 with codes AB ABBAB .4145. The periodic ABBAB usually beats the random mix, even near the reported best random chance.
